---
title: "SURE for Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage: fixed target (Level 0) and scaled identity (Level 1)"
format: html
editor: visual
---

```{r Package}

# Load required packages
library(tidyverse)
library(MASS)         # for mvrnorm (multivariate normal sampling)

set.seed(2026)
```

```{r Parameter}

# ---- Model -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Daily return vectors x_t ~ N(0, Sigma), i.i.d., known zero mean, T days, N stocks.
# No market series is needed: neither target uses it.

N <- 20
T_days <- 40
b <- runif(N, 0.5, 1.5)            # loadings for the structured part
d <- runif(N, 0.5, 1.5)            # variances for the structured part

# Family of true covariances: c = 0 gives Sigma = I (both targets exactly right),
# larger c moves Sigma away from I toward a structured matrix G.
G <- 0.5 * outer(b, b) + diag(d)
make_sigma <- function(c) (1 - c) * diag(N) + c * G

Sigma <- make_sigma(0.5)

# ---- Simulate one data set -----------------------------------------------
simulate_returns <- function(T_days, Sigma) {
  mvrnorm(n = T_days, mu = rep(0, nrow(Sigma)), Sigma = Sigma)
}

# ---- Targets ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Level 0: a fixed target chosen before seeing the data (the identity)
fixed_target <- function(S) diag(nrow(S))

# Level 1: scaled identity nu * I with nu = tr(S) / N
scaled_target <- function(S) (sum(diag(S)) / nrow(S)) * diag(nrow(S))

# ---- Shrinkage function ------------------------------------------------------
shrinkage_function <- function(S, F, alpha) {
  alpha * F + (1 - alpha) * S
}

# One sample, and check that it shrinks
X <- simulate_returns(T_days, Sigma)
S <- crossprod(X) / T_days
F1 <- scaled_target(S)
Sigma_hat <- shrinkage_function(S, F1, alpha = 0.5)
round(S[1:4, 1:4], 3)             # sample covariance
round(F1[1:4, 1:4], 3)            # scaled-identity target
round(Sigma_hat[1:4, 1:4], 3)     # shrunk: halfway between S and F
rm(X, S, F1, Sigma_hat)
```

```{r SURE_function}

# Unbiased estimates shared by both levels (Section 4, Step 3)
#   Vhat = sum_ij Varhat(s_ij) = [T (tr S)^2 + (T - 2) tr(S^2)] / [(T + 2)(T - 1)]
#   bhat = unbiased estimate of tr(Sigma^2) = T [T tr(S^2) - (tr S)^2] / [(T + 2)(T - 1)]
sure_terms <- function(X, level) {
  T_days <- nrow(X); N <- ncol(X)
  S <- crossprod(X) / T_days
  trS <- sum(diag(S)); trS2 <- sum(S^2)
  V  <- (T_days * trS^2 + (T_days - 2) * trS2) / ((T_days + 2) * (T_days - 1))
  bh <- T_days * (T_days * trS2 - trS^2) / ((T_days + 2) * (T_days - 1))
  if (level == 0) {
    F  <- fixed_target(S)
    Cv <- 0                                   # Level 0: Cov(f_ij, s_ij) = 0
  } else {
    F  <- scaled_target(S)
    Cv <- 2 * bh / (N * T_days)               # Level 1: estimate of 2 tr(Sigma^2) / (N T)
  }
  list(D2 = sum((F - S)^2), V = V, Cv = Cv, S = S, F = F)
}

sure_value <- function(terms, alpha) {
  alpha^2 * terms$D2 + (1 - 2 * alpha) * terms$V + 2 * alpha * terms$Cv
}

# SURE-chosen alpha: minimizer of the quadratic, kept in [0, 1]
sure_alpha <- function(terms) {
  min(max((terms$V - terms$Cv) / terms$D2, 0), 1)
}
```

```{r Expectation}

# Closed-form true risk R(alpha) = E||alpha F + (1 - alpha) S - Sigma||^2
true_risk <- function(alpha, Sigma, T_days, level) {
  N <- nrow(Sigma)
  trS <- sum(diag(Sigma)); trS2 <- sum(Sigma^2)
  V <- (trS^2 + trS2) / T_days                                    # sum Var(s_ij)
  if (level == 0) {
    C   <- 0
    EFS <- sum((diag(N) - Sigma)^2) + V                           # E||I - S||^2
  } else {
    C   <- 2 * trS2 / (N * T_days)                                # sum Cov(f_ij, s_ij)
    EFS <- trS2 + V - trS^2 / N - 2 * trS2 / (N * T_days)         # E||nu I - S||^2
  }
  alpha^2 * EFS + (1 - 2 * alpha) * V + 2 * alpha * C
}

oracle_alpha <- function(Sigma, T_days, level) {
  r0 <- true_risk(0, Sigma, T_days, level)
  r1 <- true_risk(1, Sigma, T_days, level)
  rh <- true_risk(0.5, Sigma, T_days, level)
  c2 <- 2 * (r1 + r0 - 2 * rh); c1 <- r1 - r0 - c2
  min(max(-c1 / (2 * c2), 0), 1)
}

# Distance of the truth from the target's structure (the x-axis)
misspecification <- function(Sigma, level) {
  N <- nrow(Sigma)
  if (level == 0) sum((Sigma - diag(N))^2)
  else sum((Sigma - (sum(diag(Sigma)) / N) * diag(N))^2)
}
```

```{r Iteration_one_setting}

# Empirical check at one setting: average true loss vs average SURE vs closed-form risk
n <- 20000
alpha <- 0.5
for (level in c(0, 1)) {
  total_error <- 0; total_sure <- 0
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    st <- sure_terms(simulate_returns(T_days, Sigma), level)
    total_error <- total_error + sum((shrinkage_function(st$S, st$F, alpha) - Sigma)^2)
    total_sure  <- total_sure + sure_value(st, alpha)
  }
  cat("Level", level, ": empirical", round(total_error / n, 4),
      " average SURE", round(total_sure / n, 4),
      " closed form", round(true_risk(alpha, Sigma, T_days, level), 4), "\n")
}
rm(level, i, st, total_error, total_sure)
```

```{r Iteration_over_misspecification}

# Performance curve: loop over how far the truth is from the target
cs <- seq(0, 1, by = 1/6)
n_samples <- 5000
Performance <- tibble()

for (level in c(0, 1)) {
  for (c in cs) {
    Sigma_c <- make_sigma(c)
    a_star  <- oracle_alpha(Sigma_c, T_days, level)
    loss_sure <- 0; total_error <- 0; total_sure <- 0
    for (i in seq_len(n_samples)) {
      st <- sure_terms(simulate_returns(T_days, Sigma_c), level)
      loss_sure   <- loss_sure + sum((shrinkage_function(st$S, st$F, sure_alpha(st)) - Sigma_c)^2)
      total_error <- total_error + sum((shrinkage_function(st$S, st$F, a_star) - Sigma_c)^2)
      total_sure  <- total_sure + sure_value(st, a_star)
    }
    Performance <- bind_rows(Performance, tibble(
      Level = ifelse(level == 0, "Level 0: fixed target I", "Level 1: scaled identity"),
      c = c,
      Misspecification = misspecification(Sigma_c, level),
      Risk_S = true_risk(0, Sigma_c, T_days, level),
      Risk_F = true_risk(1, Sigma_c, T_days, level),
      Risk_oracle = true_risk(a_star, Sigma_c, T_days, level),
      Risk_SURE_tuned = loss_sure / n_samples,
      Expected_error = true_risk(a_star, Sigma_c, T_days, level),
      Empirical_Error = total_error / n_samples,
      Average_SURE = total_sure / n_samples))
  }
}
rm(level, c, Sigma_c, a_star, loss_sure, total_error, total_sure, i, st)

Performance
```

```{r}
# Analysis: does SURE track the expected error at every setting?

Performance |>
  mutate(SURE_Diff = Average_SURE - Expected_error,
         Empirical_Diff = Empirical_Error - Expected_error) |>
  pivot_longer(c(SURE_Diff, Empirical_Diff), names_to = "Comparison", values_to = "Diff") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Misspecification, y = Diff, color = Comparison)) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
    facet_wrap(~ Level, scales = "free_x") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(SURE_Diff = "#2a78d6", Empirical_Diff = "#eb6834")) +
    labs(title = "Difference from the closed-form risk vs misspecification",
         x = "Misspecification (squared distance of Sigma from the target's structure)",
         y = "Difference from expected error") +
    theme_minimal()
ggsave("out/levels01_diff_vs_misspec.png", width = 9, height = 4, dpi = 160)
```

```{r}
# Performance curve: risk vs how far the truth is from the target

Performance |>
  dplyr::select(Level, Misspecification, Risk_S, Risk_F, Risk_oracle, Risk_SURE_tuned) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(Level, Misspecification), names_to = "Estimator", values_to = "Risk") |>
  mutate(Estimator = recode(Estimator,
                            Risk_S = "Sample covariance S",
                            Risk_F = "Target F",
                            Risk_oracle = "Oracle alpha",
                            Risk_SURE_tuned = "SURE-chosen alpha")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Misspecification, y = Risk, color = Estimator)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    facet_wrap(~ Level, scales = "free") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Sample covariance S" = "#eb6834",
                                  "Target F" = "#1baf7a",
                                  "Oracle alpha" = "#0b0b0b",
                                  "SURE-chosen alpha" = "#2a78d6")) +
    labs(title = "Performance curves",
         x = "Misspecification (squared distance of Sigma from the target's structure)",
         y = "Frobenius risk (MSE)") +
    theme_minimal()
ggsave("out/levels01_performance_curve.png", width = 9, height = 4, dpi = 160)
```

```{r Level0_SRP_style}

# ---- Level 0 in the style of the James-Stein experiment ---------------------
# With the fixed target I, the risk depends on Sigma only through its eigenvalues
# (rotating the data leaves I unchanged), just as the James-Stein risk depends on theta only
# through ||theta||. So we use a spiked covariance Sigma = I + delta * v v':
# one eigenvalue 1 + delta (a market factor), the rest equal to 1.
# x-axis: delta = ||Sigma - I||_F, the distance from the target (the analogue of ||theta||).
# One curve per dimension N, as with different p in the James-Stein experiment.

dims   <- c(5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200)
deltas <- 0:10
n_samples <- 3000
Spike <- tibble()

for (N_k in dims) {
  for (delta in deltas) {
    Sigma_k <- diag(N_k); Sigma_k[1, 1] <- 1 + delta        # v = first coordinate (direction does not matter)
    a_star  <- oracle_alpha(Sigma_k, T_days, level = 0)
    loss_sure <- 0; total_sure <- 0
    for (i in seq_len(n_samples)) {
      X  <- matrix(rnorm(T_days * N_k), T_days, N_k)
      X[, 1] <- X[, 1] * sqrt(1 + delta)
      st <- sure_terms(X, level = 0)
      loss_sure  <- loss_sure + sum((shrinkage_function(st$S, st$F, sure_alpha(st)) - Sigma_k)^2)
      total_sure <- total_sure + sure_value(st, a_star)
    }
    Spike <- bind_rows(Spike, tibble(
      N = N_k, delta = delta,
      Risk_S = true_risk(0, Sigma_k, T_days, 0),
      Risk_F = true_risk(1, Sigma_k, T_days, 0),
      Risk_oracle = true_risk(a_star, Sigma_k, T_days, 0),
      Risk_SURE_tuned = loss_sure / n_samples,
      Average_SURE = total_sure / n_samples))
  }
}
rm(N_k, delta, Sigma_k, a_star, loss_sure, total_sure, i, X, st)

Spike
```

```{r}
# Performance curves by dimension: risk vs distance from the target

Spike |>
  dplyr::select(N, delta, Risk_S, Risk_F, Risk_oracle, Risk_SURE_tuned) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(N, delta), names_to = "Estimator", values_to = "Risk") |>
  mutate(Estimator = recode(Estimator,
                            Risk_S = "Sample covariance S",
                            Risk_F = "Target I",
                            Risk_oracle = "Oracle alpha",
                            Risk_SURE_tuned = "SURE-chosen alpha"),
         N = paste("N =", N) |> fct_inorder()) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = delta, y = Risk, color = Estimator)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    facet_wrap(~ N, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Sample covariance S" = "#eb6834",
                                  "Target I" = "#1baf7a",
                                  "Oracle alpha" = "#0b0b0b",
                                  "SURE-chosen alpha" = "#2a78d6")) +
    labs(title = "Level 0 (fixed target I): performance curves by dimension",
         x = "Distance from the target, ||Sigma - I||_F (spike size delta)",
         y = "Frobenius risk (MSE)") +
    theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
ggsave("out/level0_performance_by_dim.png", width = 11, height = 4, dpi = 160)
```

```{r}
# Relative risk of SURE-chosen shrinkage vs the sample covariance, one line per dimension
# (below 1 = shrinkage helps), as in the James-Stein risk-ratio plot

Spike |>
  mutate(Ratio = Risk_SURE_tuned / Risk_S, N = factor(N)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = delta, y = Ratio, color = N)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("5" = "#c6dcf7", "10" = "#9ec5f4", "20" = "#5b9be6", "50" = "#2a78d6", "100" = "#1a56a8", "200" = "#0b2f5e")) +
    labs(title = "Level 0: risk of SURE-chosen shrinkage relative to S",
         x = "Distance from the target, ||Sigma - I||_F (spike size delta)",
         y = "Risk ratio (SURE-chosen / S)", color = "Dimension N") +
    theme_minimal()
ggsave("out/level0_risk_ratio_by_dim.png", width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 160)
```
